_readme: Answers for Install-NeologikEnvironment.ps1. Copy this file to 'inputs.json' beside the script, or give its path with -AnswerFile. Each value becomes the default of its question: press Enter to accept it, or type another value. Replace every REPLACE_ME value before use. Remove a field to be asked for it, or to accept its standard value. Acceptance of the terms, module installation and sign-in are always asked at the prompt and are never read from this file. For an unattended run (-NonInteractive), organizationCode, organizationName and fqdn must be present, and the terms are accepted with -AcceptTerms. Entries that begin with an underscore are notes and are ignored.
organizationCode: REPLACE_ME - your three-character organisation code, lower case, for example abc
organizationName: REPLACE_ME - your organisation's full name, for example Contoso Ltd
fqdn: REPLACE_ME - the environment's fully qualified host name, for example neologik.contoso.com
_documentAnalysisRegion_note: The Azure region for document analysis, agreed with Neologik. Choose one of australiaeast, canadacentral, eastus, eastus2, japaneast, southcentralus, southeastasia, swedencentral, uksouth, westeurope, westus and westus3. Leave the field empty to use azureRegion, when azureRegion is on that list.
_resourceTags_note: applyResourceTags true (the default) tags every Azure resource the script creates with Vendor, ApplicationName, ManagedBy, Environment, Solution and DeploymentDate. Choose true if your Azure Policies refuse untagged resources. resourceTagsCustom holds optional tags of your own, as an object or as a string of the form Key=Value,Key2=Value2. Keys use letters, digits, full stops, underscores and hyphens; values contain no comma and no equals sign. A custom tag replaces a standard tag of the same name. Ignored when applyResourceTags is false.
_naming_note: Optional names of your own. Leave a field empty, or remove it, to accept the standard name. solutionName: neo-<org><env>-<region>-<index>, for example neo-abcprd-uks-01. solutionShortName: <org><env><index>, for example abcprd01; it also forms the suffix of the security group, application and managed identity names. keyVaultName: 3 to 24 characters, letters, digits and hyphens, beginning with a letter. storageAccountName: 3 to 24 characters, lower-case letters and digits. scriptRunnerIdentityName, sqlIdentityName, directoryIdentityName and systemTaskIdentityName: 3 to 128 characters, letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, beginning with a letter or digit. directoryIdentityName names the agent registration identity. systemTaskIdentityName names the system task managed identity.
_existingAccounts_note: Read only when skipGuestInvitation is true. addExistingAccountsToGroups true adds accounts you have already created, as guests or as members, to the security groups, and sends no invitation. existingAccountEmails lists their addresses; when it is omitted, the addresses in NeologikGuestUsers.txt are used. Each address must match the account's mail address or user principal name exactly. An address with no matching account is reported and passed over. Accounts added in this way join all four Neologik security groups, including the Admin User Group, which carries Azure administration rights on the resource group.
_existingServicePrincipalSecret_note: The -ExistingServicePrincipalSecret parameter is preferable to this field, because it keeps the client secret out of this file. Leave the field empty to be asked for the secret, or to add it to the Key Vault yourself.
_agents_note: Agents are created in the Neologik Admin Tool after the environment is deployed. The onboarding script asks nothing about them.
